_comment: v1 schema for LLM-extracted per-task fields (stage 05). Each field is an ORTHOGONAL axis: activity_type = what you physically DO; judging_criterion = how the winner is DECIDED; task_twist = the gimmick/constraint (multi, usually a short list or empty); key_props = notable objects (hover flavour only, never a colormap). Do not reuse a slug from one field as the value for another. Slugs are deliberately fan-legible (they become colormap categories and filters). Expect to iterate this against a ~50-task sample before the full run, the way the sibling huggingface-dataset-map taxonomy was iterated.

activity_type._note: Single-select. The headline 'what kind of task is this'. Pick the dominant act; if a task both builds and performs, choose the one the brief foregrounds.

categories.name: make-or-build
categories.description: Create or construct a physical thing: draw, paint, sculpt, build a contraption, assemble, design, cook-as-craft. The core act is making an object or artwork that will be looked at.

categories.name: performance
categories.description: Perform for the camera or studio: sing, dance, act, do an impression, tell a joke, put on a show, deliver a routine, stunt. The core act is a performance watched by others.

categories.name: physical-feat
categories.description: An athletic or dexterity challenge: throw, catch, aim, roll, balance, race, jump, lift, hit a target. The core act is bodily skill or coordination.

categories.name: food-and-drink
categories.description: Eat, drink, taste, identify, or prepare food and drink. Includes consuming as much/as fast as possible, blind taste tests, and assembling edible things judged as food.

categories.name: mental-puzzle
categories.description: Solve a problem with your head: a riddle, code, sum, logic puzzle, memory feat, quiz, or planning challenge. The core act is figuring something out.

categories.name: find-or-acquire
categories.description: Bring, find, fetch, collect, or retrieve items — including prize-task 'bring the most/best X' briefs and treasure-hunt searches. The core act is sourcing or gathering things.

categories.name: social-mission
categories.description: Use other people as the medium: persuade, recruit, instruct, prank, or get a member of the public or a helper to do something. The core act is influencing other people (distinct from deceive-the-taskmaster, which targets Alex/Greg).

categories.name: deceive-alex-or-greg
categories.description: Trick, fool, surprise, sneak past, smuggle, or mislead Alex Horne (in filmed tasks — the most common case) or Greg the Taskmaster (in the studio). The core act is pulling something over on them, not on other people (which is social-mission).

categories.name: endurance-or-wait
categories.description: Wait, endure, persist, or do nothing well: be the last to act, hold a pose, kill time, sustain an effort. The core act is patience or stamina rather than a discrete deed.

categories.name: other
categories.description: A clearly-described task that genuinely fits none of the activities above.

categories.name: not_stated
categories.description: The brief is too terse to tell what you actually do.

judging_criterion._note: Single-select. How the winner is decided — the measuring stick, not the activity. A 'make' task can be judged subjective-best OR fastest; keep this independent of activity_type.

categories.name: fastest
categories.description: Ranked by speed: least time taken, or first to finish.

categories.name: most-quantity
categories.description: Ranked by amount or count: most items, biggest number, as much as possible.

categories.name: furthest-or-highest
categories.description: Ranked by distance, height, or extent of a single result: throw furthest, build tallest, travel furthest.

categories.name: most-accurate
categories.description: Ranked by precision or correctness: closest to a target, most right answers, neatest, least error.

categories.name: subjective-best
categories.description: Ranked by the Taskmaster's taste: 'best', 'most beautiful', 'most impressive'. A quality judgement, not a measurement.

categories.name: funniest
categories.description: Ranked on humour or entertainment value: 'funniest', 'most amusing'.

categories.name: most-surprising
categories.description: Ranked on surprise, originality, or unexpectedness: 'most surprising', 'most unexpected', 'most unusual'.

categories.name: completion-binary
categories.description: Pass/fail or did-you-manage-it: success is completing the task at all, not out-scoring others on a scale.

categories.name: other
categories.description: A clearly-stated basis for judging that fits none of the above.

categories.name: not_stated
categories.description: The brief doesn't say how it's judged.

task_twist._note: Multi-select LIST — most tasks return [] or one slug. Only add a slug when the brief makes the constraint explicit and central. Never invent slugs outside this list.
task_twist.rule: Return a JSON list of zero or more applicable slugs. If no twist applies, return []. Do not use 'not_stated' for this field.

categories.name: time-limit
categories.description: An explicit clock or countdown constrains the task ('you have 60 seconds', 'in 20 minutes').

categories.name: single-attempt
categories.description: Exactly one go is allowed — no retries, one shot.

categories.name: do-x-whilst-y
categories.description: Two things must happen at once: do the main task whilst also doing or holding something else ('paint a horse whilst riding a horse').

categories.name: blindfold-sensory
categories.description: A sense is deliberately removed: blindfolded, earmuffs, in the dark, can't see/hear.

categories.name: body-restriction
categories.description: Use of the body is restricted: no hands, one leg, tied up, can't use a named body part.

categories.name: teamwork
categories.description: The task is done as a team or pair rather than solo.

categories.name: uses-alex
categories.description: Alex Horne (or another helper) is a required part of the task — you direct, use, or depend on him.

categories.name: secret-reveal
categories.description: There's a hidden rule, secret instruction, or surprise twist revealed during or after the task.

categories.name: members-of-public
categories.description: Members of the public (strangers — not the contestants, Alex, or Greg) are involved.

key_props._note: Open list, HOVER-ONLY (never a colormap). The distinctive objects that give a task its flavour.
key_props.rule: Return a JSON list of up to 3 short noun phrases for the most notable physical objects, props, or materials the task centres on (e.g. ['watermelon'], ['horse','easel'], ['balloon','egg']). Lowercase, singular where natural. Return [] for tasks with no distinctive prop (pure mental or social tasks).
